plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes crowded with fragrant violet-blue blossoms. Bees and butterflies swarm the fields, and the scent drifts for miles on warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer, peaking in late June through July
plants.location: Provence, France, and the wider Mediterranean and temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nymphaea caerulea
plants.description: Star-shaped sky-blue petals rise above round floating pads and open to golden centers. The flowers open in the morning sun and close again by afternoon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Warm months, with strong flowering in the summer rains of tropical and subtropical Africa
plants.location: Nile Valley and tropical East and Southern Africa
plants.funFact: Ancient Egyptians painted and carved this flower in tombs and temples. They treated it as a symbol of rebirth and the rising sun.

plants.name: Banksia ericifolia
plants.description: Bottle-brush spikes of glowing orange-gold rise from fine, needle-like foliage. Honeyeaters and lorikeets crowd the nectar-rich blooms in the cool Southern Hemisphere winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to winter, peaking from about May to July
plants.location: Coastal sandstone heathlands of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: Each cone-like spike is made of thousands of tiny flowers. After fire, the woody cones can open and release their seeds.
